items.readable_text:
Content:
An ellipse is a circle that has been stretched. For example, let's look at the ellipse given below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/3a2a913fc89e69e7939f83d4c35ae042]

Content:
The longest diameter of an ellipse is called the major axis.

Content:
So, for the ellipse above, the major axis is the line segment bounded by the points [MATH: (1,-2)] and [MATH: (1,4),] and its length is [MATH: 4-(-2)=6.]

Content:
Half of the major axis is called a semi-major axis. For our ellipse above, the length of the semi-major axis is [MATH: \dfrac{6}{2} = 3.]

Content:
On the other hand, the minor axis is the shortest diameter of an ellipse.
Let's have another look at the same ellipse:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/fe45be387514f1aff084879219f783e5]

Content:
Here, we see the minor axis of the ellipse. It is the line segment bounded by the points [MATH: (-1,1)] and [MATH: (3,1),] and its length is [MATH: 3-(-1)=4.]

Content:
Half of the minor axis is called a semi-minor axis. For our ellipse, the semi-minor axis has a length of [MATH: \dfrac{4}{2} = 2.]

Content:
For this particular ellipse:

Content:
- Since the major axis is parallel to the [MATH: y]-axis, the major axis is said to be "along the [MATH: y]-direction".
- Since the minor axis is parallel to the [MATH: x]-axis, the minor axis is said to be "along the [MATH: x]-direction".

Content:
Note that for other ellipses, it may be opposite: the major axis may be along the [MATH: x]-direction, and the minor axis may be along the [MATH: y]-direction.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
An ellipse is a circle that has been stretched. For example, let's look at the ellipse given below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/3a2a913fc89e69e7939f83d4c35ae042]

Content:
The longest diameter of an ellipse is called the major axis.

Content:
So, for the ellipse above, the major axis is the line segment bounded by the points [MATH: (1,-2)] and [MATH: (1,4),] and its length is [MATH: 4-(-2)=6.]

Content:
Half of the major axis is called a semi-major axis. For our ellipse above, the length of the semi-major axis is [MATH: \dfrac{6}{2} = 3.]

Content:
On the other hand, the minor axis is the shortest diameter of an ellipse.
Let's have another look at the same ellipse:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/fe45be387514f1aff084879219f783e5]

Content:
Here, we see the minor axis of the ellipse. It is the line segment bounded by the points [MATH: (-1,1)] and [MATH: (3,1),] and its length is [MATH: 3-(-1)=4.]

Content:
Half of the minor axis is called a semi-minor axis. For our ellipse, the semi-minor axis has a length of [MATH: \dfrac{4}{2} = 2.]

Content:
For this particular ellipse:

Content:
- Since the major axis is parallel to the [MATH: y]-axis, the major axis is said to be "along the [MATH: y]-direction".
- Since the minor axis is parallel to the [MATH: x]-axis, the minor axis is said to be "along the [MATH: x]-direction".

Content:
Note that for other ellipses, it may be opposite: the major axis may be along the [MATH: x]-direction, and the minor axis may be along the [MATH: y]-direction.

Item 2 — Example: Determining the Lengths of the Major and Minor Axes of an Ellipse

Example Prompt:
What are the lengths of the major and minor axes of the ellipse given below?

[IMG: /graphics/f800398f09f7c8e4a7d629ceae4476f1]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The major axis is the longest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points [MATH: (-3,1)] and [MATH: (7,1).] So, the length of the major axis is [MATH: 7 - (-3) = 10.]

The minor axis is the shortest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points [MATH: (2,-1)] and [MATH: (2,3).] So, the length of the minor axis is [MATH: 3 - (-1) = 4.]
